title: Quantized Hyperfine Field at an Implanted $μ^+$ Site in PrPb$_3$: Interplay between Localized $f$ Electrons and an Interstitial Charged Particle
authors: T. U. Ito, W. Higemoto, K. Ohishi, N. Nishida, R. H. Heffner, Y. Aoki, A. Amato, T. Onimaru, H. S. Suzuki
abstract: The local effect of an interstitial hydrogen-like particle on localized $f$ electrons was studied in PrPb$_3$ by means of $μ^+$ spin rotation and relaxation. Spontaneous $μ^+$ spin precession with harmonic frequencies was observed for the first time in $f$ electron compounds. We demonstrate that the signal is derived from a coupling between the $μ^+$ spin and the hyperfine-enhanced nuclear spin of nearest neighbor (nn) $^{141}$Pr with Ising-like anisotropy. The signal also suggests a marked suppression of spin dynamics of the nn $^{141}$Pr in comparison with that of the bulk $^{141}$Pr. These facts strongly indicate modification of the $f$ electronic state due to the interstitial charged particle.
summary: This work uses mu+SR to study how an implanted mu+ particle modifies the electronic state of localized f electrons in PrPb3. Key findings include observing quantized mu+ spin precession frequencies, which confirm a strong, anisotropic coupling between the mu+ spin and the Pr nuclear spins. This provides microscopic evidence of the interplay between interstitial impurities and localized magnetic moments.
main_problem: The study investigates the local magnetic effect of an implanted mu+ particle on localized f electrons in PrPb3, focusing on the interplay between the mu+ spin and the hyperfine-enhanced nuclear spin of nearest neighbor Pr ions.
main_result: Spontaneous mu+ spin precession with harmonic frequencies was observed for the first time in f electron compounds, indicating a quantized hyperfine field arising from coupling between the mu+ spin and the Pr nuclear spin.
method: The research utilizes Positive Muon Spin Rotation and Relaxation (mu+SR) measurements to probe the local magnetic environment.
model_or_system: The system is PrPb3 containing an interstitial mu+. The physics is modeled using a spin Hamiltonian incorporating hyperfine coupling terms (H_SI) that exhibit Ising-like anisotropy.
key_observables: Mu+ spin precession frequencies (f_i), Mu+ Knight shift (K), and the time evolution of the muon polarization P(t).
important_parameters: The hyperfine field (HF) at the mu+ site is found to be quantized, and the coupling constant a_J is estimated to be around 10^5 mK.
main_assumptions: The mu+ influence is assumed to affect only the nearest neighbor Pr ions, and the analysis relies on fitting the muon relaxation function to a sum of cosine terms.
figures_summary: The notes mention fitting the muon polarization decay to a sum of cosine terms yielding five harmonic frequencies, and a linear fit of the fundamental frequency versus the measured K_parallel.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system and the mu+SR technique, to developing the spin Hamiltonian describing the coupling, and finally presenting the key results showing quantized precession frequencies and the derived hyperfine field.
why_interesting: The observation of quantized spin dynamics and the detailed analysis of the spin Hamiltonian provide insights into strong local magnetic interactions and crystal field effects in rare-earth compounds, which are central to correlated electron physics.
